# Handlers

A handler is **any process** that reads from stdin and writes to stdout. The runtime forks a fresh process for every tuple. No persistent state in the handler. No memory leaks. No OOM.

```
read payload bytes from stdin
do work
write result bytes to stdout
exit
```

## Examples

A shell script is a fully valid handler:

```sh
#!/bin/sh
payload=$(cat)
curl -s https://api.example.com/v1/query \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -d "$payload" \
  | jq -c '{answer:.result}'
```

A zero-alloc C handler:

```c
static char g_in[256 * 1024];
static char g_out[256 * 1024];

int main(void) {
    size_t n = fread(g_in, 1, sizeof(g_in) - 1, stdin);
    g_in[n] = '\0';
    // ... process ...
    fputs(g_out, stdout);
}
```

```{=html}
  <div class="card"><h3>Python / WASM</h3><p>Full standard library for rapid iteration. Sandboxed determinism with WASM.</p></div>
</div>
```

## Header env vars

The runtime sets these environment variables before forking every handler:

```{=html}
<div class="env-table">
  <div class="env-row"><div class="env-key">ACTOR_TUPLE_ID</div><div class="env-val">Hex ID of the incoming tuple.</div></div>
  <div class="env-row"><div class="env-key">ACTOR_CORRELATION_ID</div><div class="env-val">Hex correlation ID — stable across the entire causal chain.</div></div>
  <div class="env-row"><div class="env-key">ACTOR_CAUSATION_ID</div><div class="env-val">Hex ID of the direct parent tuple.</div></div>
  <div class="env-row"><div class="env-key">ACTOR_TUPLE_ORIGIN</div><div class="env-val">Actor ID that emitted the incoming tuple.</div></div>
  <div class="env-row"><div class="env-key">ACTOR_ATTEMPT</div><div class="env-val">Retry count. 0 on first delivery.</div></div>
</div>
```

A shell handler reads them as ordinary environment variables:

```sh
#!/bin/sh
echo "handling tuple $ACTOR_TUPLE_ID attempt $ACTOR_ATTEMPT" >&2
payload=$(cat)
# ...
```

## Dynamic result routing

By default the runtime publishes handler output on `ACTOR_RESULT_TOPIC`. A handler overrides this by writing a topic name as the first line of stdout:

```
sql_query
{"type":"sql_query","sql":"SELECT ..."}
```

The runtime strips the first line and publishes the payload on that topic. One handler can fan out to multiple downstream actors without any runtime change.
